The first reaction is key in radiocarbon dating (see Section 19.4). 32P is commonly used as a radiotracer in biology to follow biological reactions involving phospho- rus, and 90Sr is one of the longer-lived radioactive isotopes still present in Belarus following the disastrous explosion of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant.
Proton-rich nuclei may decay by emitting 1 particles as an alternative to a decay. A proton is converted to a neutron, leading to the emission of a high-energy posi- tron ( 1

0e+ ) and a neutrino (n), as shown in Figure 19.7. The mass number A of the daughter nuclide is unchanged, but the atomic number Z has decreased by 1. The kinetic energy (DE) is distributed between the positron and the neutrino.
